questions.q: If $A$~and~$B$ are two non-zero~$n \times n$ matrices such that~$A^{2} + B = A^{2}B,$ then
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

$A^{2}B = A^{2} + B$

$⇒ A^{2}B - A^{2} - B + I = I$

$⇒ A^{2}\left(B - I\right) - \left(B - I\right) = I$

$⇒ \left(A^{2} - I\right)\left(B - I\right) = I$

$⇒ \left(A^{2} - I\right)\left(B - I\right)\left(B - I\right)- 1 = I\left(B - I\right)- 1$

$⇒ \left(A^{2} - I\right) = \left(B - I\right)- 1$

Also,

$A^{2} + B = A^{2}B$

$⇒ A^{2} \left(B - I\right) = B$

$⇒ A^{2} = B\left(B - I\right)- 1$

$⇒ A^{2} = B\left(A^{2} - I\right)$

$⇒ A^{2} = BA^{2} - B$

$⇒ A^{2} + B = BA^{2}$

$⇒ A^{2}B = BA^{2}

$

questions.q: If $A = \left[\begin{cases}cos\theta & - sin\theta \\ sin\theta & cos\theta\end{cases}\right]$ , then the matrix $A^{- 50}$ when $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{12},$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$A = \left[\begin{cases}cos\theta & - sin\theta \\ sin\theta & cos\theta\end{cases}\right] ⇒ \left|A\right| = \left|\begin{cases}cos\theta & - sin\theta \\ sin\theta & cos\theta\end{cases}\right| = \cos^{2}\theta + \sin^{2}\theta = 1$

And $adj\left(A\right) = \left[\begin{cases}cos\theta & sin\theta \\ - sin\theta & cos\theta\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ A^{- 1} = \dfrac{1}{\left|A\right|}adj\left(A\right) = \left[\begin{cases}cos\theta & sin\theta \\ - sin\theta & cos\theta\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ A^{- 2} = { \left(A^{- 1}\right)}^{2} = \left($A^{- 1}\right)\left(A^{- 1}\right)$

$= \left[\b$bbegin{cases}cos\theta$ \text{ and } $sin\theta$\\ - $sin\theta$ \text{ and } $cos\theta\end{cases}\right] \left[\b$bbegin{cases}cos\theta& sin\theta\\ - sin\theta& cos\theta\end{cases}\right]$

$= \left[\begin{cases}\cos^{2}\theta - \sin^{2}\theta \text{ and } 2sin\thetacos\theta\\ - 2sin\$thetacos\theta$ \text{ and } $\cos^{2}\theta -sin2\theta\end{cases}\right]

$= \left[\bbegin{cases}cos2\theta \text{ and } sin2\theta\\ - sin2\theta \text{ and } cos2\theta\end{cases}\right]$

It is visible that

${\left(A^{- 1}\right)}^{n} = \left[\bbegin{cases}cosn\theta$ \text{ and } $sinn\theta$\\ - $sinn\theta$ \text{ and } $cosn\theta\end{cases}\right]

$⇒ A^{- 50} = ${\left($A^{- 1}\right)}^{50} = \left[\bbegin{cases}cos50\theta \text{ and } sin50\theta\\ - sin50\theta \text{ and } cos50\theta\end{cases}\right]$

Now at $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{12},sin50\theta ==sin\dfrac{50\pi}{12} ===sin\dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}

$cos50\theta $==cos\dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$⇒ A^{- 50} = \left[\begin{cases}\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ \text{ and } $\dfrac{1}{2}$\\ $\dfrac{- 1}{2}$ \text{ and } \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\end{cases}\right]$$

questions.q: Let $A$ be a symmetric matrix of order $2$ with integer entries. If the sum of the diagonal elements of $A^{2}$ is $1,$ then the possible number of such matrices is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$A = \left(\begin{cases}a & b \\ b & c\end{cases}\right), a, b, c \in I$

$A^{2} = \left(\begin{cases}a & b \\ b & c\end{cases}\right)\left(\begin{cases}a & b \\ b & c\end{cases}\right) = \left(\begin{cases}a^{2} + b^{2} & b\left(a + c\right) \\ b\left(a + c\right) & b^{2} + c^{2}\end{cases}\right)$

Sum of the diagonal entries of

$A^{2} = a^{2} + 2b^{2} + c^{2}$

Given $a^{2} + 2b^{2} + c^{2} = 1, a, b, c \in I$

$b = 0 \text{ and } a^{2} + c^{2} = 1$

Case-1:~$a = 0 ⇒ c = \pm 1$ ($2$-matrices)

Case-2: $c = 0 ⇒ a = \pm 1$ ($2$-matrices)

Total $= 4$ matrices

questions.subject: Mathematics

Here,& $\alpha = \omega, {ω}^{2}$~where~$\omega$~is complex cube root of unity.

$A^{2} = \dfrac{1}{3}\left[\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & \omega & {ω}^{2} \\ 1 & {ω}^{2} & \omega\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & \omega & {ω}^{2} \\ 1 & {ω}^{2} & \omega\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ A^{4} = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ A^{31} = A^{28} \times A^{3} = I \times A^{3} = A^{3}$

questions.q: If $A$ is a symmetric matrix and $B$ is skew- symmetric matrix such that $A + B = \left[\begin{cases}2 & 3 \\ 5 & - 1\end{cases}\right]$ , then $AB$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given $A$ is symmetric and $B$ is skew symmetric, hence~
$A = \left[\begin{cases}a & b \\ b & c\end{cases}\right]$ and $B = \left[\begin{cases}0 & d \\ - d & 0\end{cases}\right]$
Now $A + B = \left[\begin{cases}a & b + d \\ b - d & c\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}2 & 3 \\ 5 & - 1\end{cases}\right]$
$⇒ a = 2, b = 4, c = - 1$ and $d = - 1$
$⇒ A = \left[\begin{cases}2 & 4 \\ 4 & - 1\end{cases}\right]$ and $B = \left[\begin{cases}0 & - 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{cases}\right]$
Hence $AB = \left[\begin{cases}2 & 4 \\ 4 & - 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}0 & - 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}4 & - 2 \\ - 1 & - 4\end{cases}\right]$

questions.q: Let $A$ be a $3 \times 3$ real matrix such that $A^2(A-2 I)-4(\mathrm{~A}-\mathrm{I})=\mathrm{O}$, where I and O are the identity and null matrices, respectively. If $A^5=\alpha A^2+\beta A+\gamma I$, where $\alpha, \beta$ and $\gamma$ are real constants, then $\alpha+\beta+\gamma$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & A^3-2 A^2-4 A+4 I=0 \\ & A^3=2 A^2+4 A-4 I \\ & A^4=2 A^3+4 A^2-4 A \\ & =2\left(2 A^2+4 A-4 I\right)+4 A^2-4 A \\ & A^4=8 A^2+4 A-8 I \\ & A^5=8 A^3+4 A^2-8 A \\ & =8\left(2 A^2+4 A-4 I\right)+4 A^2-8 A \\ & A^5=20 A^2+24 A-32 I \\ & \therefore \alpha=20, \beta=24, \gamma=-32 \\ & \therefore \alpha+\beta+\gamma=12\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $A = \left[\begin{cases}0 & - 2 \\ 2 & 0\end{cases}\right]$. If $M$~and $N$ are two matrices given by $M = \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{10}A^{2k}$~and $N = \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{10}A^{2k - 1}$~then $MN^{2}$& is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Since& $A = \left[\begin{cases}0 & - 2 \\ 2 & 0\end{cases}\right]$

So~$A^{2} = \left[\begin{cases}0 & - 2 \\ 2 & 0\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}0 & - 2 \\ 2 & 0\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}- 4 & 0 \\ 0 & - 4\end{cases}\right] = - 4I$

and~$A^{3} = - 4A$

Similarly~$A^{4} = \left(- 4I\right)\left(- 4I\right) = \left(- 4\right)2I$,~

$A^{5} = \left(- 4\right)2A, A^{6} = \left(- 4\right)3I$

Now~$M = \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{10}A^{2k} = A^{2} + A^{4} + \ldots . + A^{20}$

$= \left[- 4 + \left(- 4\right)2 + \left(- 4\right)3 + \ldots . + \left(- 4\right)20\right]I$

$= - {k}_{1}I$

So~$M$ is symmetric matrix

$N = \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{10}A^{2k - 1} = A + A^{3} + \ldots \ldots + A^{19}$

$= A \left[1 + \left(-4\right) + \left(-4\right)2 + \ldots \ldots + \left(-4\right)9\right]$

$= {k}_{2}A$

So $N$~is skew symmetric

$⇒ N^{2}$ is symmetric matrix

Hence,~$MN^{2} is non-identity symmetric matrix

$

${Δ}_{1} = \left|$\begin{cases}$2 \text{ and } - 1 \text{ and } 2 \\ - 4 \text{ and } - 2 \text{ and } \lambda \\ 4 \text{ and } \lambda \text{ and } 1\end{cases}\right| = - 2 \left({λ}^{2} +$6\lambda - 4\right)$
\Delta =$0 ⇒ \lambda = 1, - $\dfrac{1}{2}

~And for $\lambda = 1, - $\dfrac{1}{2}, {∆}_{1} \ne$0$
Hence, $S = \left$\{1, - $\dfrac{1}{2}\right$\}

$

questions.q: If $P$ is a $3 \times 3$~real matrix such that $P^{T} = aP + ( a - 1 ) I$, where $a > 1$, then
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$P^{T} = aP + ( a - 1 ) I . . . . . . ( 1 )$

Taking transpose on both sides we get,

\left(P^{T}\right)T = \left(aP + ( a - 1 ) I\right)T$

$⇒ P = aP^{T} + ( a - 1 ) I . . . . . . . ( 2 )$

Subtract equation (1) and (2),

$⇒ P^{T} - P = a \left(P - P^{T}\right)$

$⇒ P = P^{T}$~as~$a \ne - 1$

From equation (1),

$P = aP + ( a - 1 ) I$

$⇒ P = - I$

Taking adjoint on both sides,

$⇒ AdjP = Adj ( - I )$

$⇒ \left|AdjP\right| = \left|Adj ( - I )\right| = \left|-I\right|2$

$⇒ | Adj P | = 1$

$

questions.q: Let $A$ be a $3 \times 3$ matrix and $det\left(A\right) = 2$. If $n = det \left(\mathop{adj \left($adj \left(. ... \left(\leftadjA\right)\right)\right)\right) ⏟}_{2024 - times}\right), then the remainder when $n$ is divided by $9$ is equal to __________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

\left|A\right| = 2$

And $n = det \left(\mathop{adj \left($adj \left(adj . .. \left(A\right)\right)\right) ⏟}_{2024times}\right)

Now, using the formula $\mathop{\left|$adj\left($adj\left($adj . .. \left($A\right)\right)\right)\right| ⏟}_{rtimes} = \left|$A\right|\left($n - 1\right)r$ we get,

$\mathop{\mathop{adj\left($adj\left($adj . .. \left($A\right)\right)\right)}_{⏟}}_{2024times} = \left|$A\right|\left($n - 1\right)2024$

$⇒ n = \left|$A\right|{2}^{2024}$

$⇒ n = {2}^{22024}\left$\{\text{as}\left|$A\right| = 2\right\}$

Now, solving

${2}^{2024} = {4}^{1012} = \left($3 + 1\right)1012 = 3k + 1$

$⇒ {2}^{22024} = {2}^{3k + 1}$

$⇒ {2}^{22024} = 2 $\cdot {2}^{3k}

$⇒ {2}^{22024} = 2 $\cdot \left($9 - 1\right)k$

$⇒ {2}^{22024} = 9m - 2$

$⇒ {2}^{22024} = 9t - 2 + 9$

$⇒ {2}^{22024} = 9m + 7$

Hence, the remainder is $7$

we get~$⇒ $\dfrac{9 !}{6 ! 2 ! 1 !} =$252 . . . \left(ii\right)$

Now adding equation~ \left($i\right) + \left(ii\right) + \left($iii\right)$

So total~$414$ \text{ and } ways will be there. \text{ and }

questions.q: Let $A$ be a symmetric matrix such that \left|A\right| = 2$ and~\left[\begin{cases}2 & 1 \\ 3 & \dfrac{3}{2}\end{cases}\right]A = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 2 \\ \alpha & \beta\end{cases}\right]$~If the sum of the diagonal~elements of $A$ is~$s$, then $\dfrac{\betas}{\alpha2}$ is equal to _________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let

$A = \left[\begin{cases}a & b \\ b & c\end{cases}\right]$

And,

\left[\begin{cases}2 & 1 \\ 3 & \dfrac{3}{2}\end{cases}\right]A = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 2 \\ \alpha & \beta\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ \left[\begin{cases}2 & 1 \\ 3 & \dfrac{3}{2}\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}a & b \\ b & c\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 2 \\ \alpha & \beta\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ \left[\begin{cases}2a + b & 2b + c \\ 3a + \dfrac{3b}{2} & 3b + \dfrac{3c}{2}\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 2 \\ \alpha & \beta\end{cases}\right]$

So,

$2a + b = 12b + c = 2$

So,~$4a - c = 0 . . . . \left(i\right)$

Also,

\left|A\right| = 2 ⇒ ac - b^{2} = 2$

$⇒ a\left(4a\right) - \left(1 - 2a\right)2 = 2$

$⇒ 4a^{2} - 4a^{2} - 1 + 4a = 2$

$⇒ a = $\dfrac{3}{4}

$⇒ b = 1 - 2a = 1 - $\dfrac{6}{4} = - \dfrac{1}{2}

$c = 4a = 3$

And,~

$3a + $\dfrac{3b}{2} = \alpha$⇒ \alpha = $\dfrac{9}{4} - \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{3}{2}$3b + $\dfrac{3c}{2} = \beta$⇒ \beta = - $\dfrac{3}{2} + \dfrac{9}{2} =$3$

So,

$A = \left[\begin{cases}\dfrac{3}{4} \text{ and } - \dfrac{1}{2}\\ - \dfrac{1}{2} \text{ and } 3\end{cases}\right]$

So,~$Tr\left(A\right) = s = \dfrac{3}{4} +3 = \dfrac{15}{4}$

$\dfrac{\beta \times s}{\alpha2} = \dfrac{3 \times \dfrac{15}{4}}{\dfrac{9}{4}} =5

$
